detail: Records the two-storey arcaded base, six intermediary storeys, two-storey arcaded top, grey granite, Indiana limestone, truncated hipped copper roofs with fine dormers, and copper-detailed formal entry.
Winnipeg heritage survey records the four north oriels, high southern chimney and carved stone gables.
Canadian Register records the envelope, stonework, pinnacles, small shed and hip dormers and still standing entrance.
City height summary gives 59 metres above grade, consistent with the directly measured main roof and chimney range.
The original Ross & MacFarlane archival project catalog places the executed 1910–14 railway design at 222 Broadway.
